title: Montgomery GI Bill Selected Reserves Tuition Fairness Act of 2025
official_title: To Amend title 38, United States Code, to direct the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to disapprove courses of education offered by a public institution of higher learning that does not charge the in-State tuition rate to a veteran using certain educational assistance under title 10 of such Code, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Enacted as Public Law 119-55 on December 12, 2025. Per the printed legislative history for H.R. 983, the House considered and passed the measure on April 7, 2025 and the Senate considered and passed it on November 20, 2025.
summary: Extends the Department of Veterans Affairs' in-State tuition disapproval regime in section 3679(c) of title 38, United States Code, to cover educational assistance under chapter 1606 of title 10 (Montgomery GI Bill Selected Reserves). It inserts ", or chapter 1606 of title 10," after existing chapter citations in paragraph (1) and paragraph (6), adds a new subparagraph (E) covering individuals entitled to assistance under section 16131 of title 10, and makes conforming changes to subsection (e). The amendments apply to an academic period that begins on or after August 1, 2026.
brief: Extends the VA in-State tuition disapproval rule in 38 U.S.C. 3679 to Selected Reserves educational assistance under chapter 1606 of title 10, effective for academic periods beginning on or after August 1, 2026.

items.main: Names the Act the "Montgomery GI Bill Selected Reserves Tuition Fairness Act of 2025."
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Department of Veterans Affairs Disapproval of Courses Offered by Public Institutions of Higher Learning That Do Not Charge Veterans In-State Tuition Rate for Purposes of Selected Reserve Educational Assistance Program

items.main: Subsection (a) amends 38 U.S.C. 3679(c) by (1) inserting ", or chapter 1606 of title 10," after "chapter 30, 31, 33, or 35 of this title" in paragraph (1); (2) adding new subparagraph (E) to paragraph (2), covering an individual entitled to assistance under section 16131 of title 10; and (3) inserting ", or chapter 1606 of title 10" before the period at the end of paragraph (6).
items.detail: The three changes extend the disapproval rule to the chapter 1606 (Selected Reserves) program in title 10, while leaving the paragraph (2)(A)-(D) categories in place.

items.main: Subsection (b) makes conforming amendments to 38 U.S.C. 3679(e): paragraph (1)(A) adds ", or chapter 1606 of title 10," after "chapter 31, 33, or 35 of this title"; paragraph (1)(B) replaces "chapter 31 33, or 35 of this title" with "chapter 31, 33, or 35 of this title, or chapter 1606 of title 10"; paragraph (2) makes the same replacement.
items.detail: Subsection (e) references are updated so the covered-chapter lists stay parallel to the amended subsection (c).

items.main: Subsection (c) sets the effective date: amendments take effect on the date of enactment and apply with respect to an academic period that begins on or after August 1, 2026.
items.detail: The two-tier effective date lets institutions and the VA adjust before the change binds any given academic period.

gaps: The bill does not restate the in-State tuition disapproval rule itself; that mechanism is set by the surrounding text of 38 U.S.C. 3679, which is not reproduced in this Act.
The bill does not create a private right of enforcement for a Selected Reserves student denied the in-State rate.
The bill does not authorize additional funding for the VA's disapproval or oversight activities.
The bill does not describe how existing state residency policies at public institutions must be modified to comply.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Van Orden
featured_quotes.text: This bill holds particular significance for me because the issue was first brought to my attention by one of my constituents, Mr. Greg Tremelling, a fellow veteran, during our Veterans Day listening session hosted last Congress. His voice, joined by countless other reservists and veterans, highlighted the urgent need for policy change, and this is precisely what this government  should be doing: listening to our constituents and acting on their needs.

modified: 38 U.S.C. 3679(c)(1): chapter 1606 of title 10 added to the covered-chapter list
